=== py-bindings Cargo.toml ===
[package]
name = "paigasus-py-bindings"
version = "0.1.0"
edition.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
authors.workspace = true
publish = false

[lib]
# Only cdylib: Python loads this artifact; no other Rust crate consumes it.
crate-type = ["cdylib"]
# A PyO3 `extension-module` cdylib leaves libpython symbols undefined, so a Rust test
# harness for this target can't link. Kernel logic is unit-tested in `paigasus-kernel`; the
# FFI boundary is proven by compilation. Disable the (un-linkable, empty) test/doctest
# targets so `cargo nextest --no-tests=pass` stays green (SMA-409).
test = false
doctest = false

[dependencies]
pyo3.workspace = true
paigasus-kernel.workspace = true

[package.metadata.cargo-machete]
# pyo3 is consumed only through attribute macros (#[pyfunction]/#[pymodule]) — the canonical
# cargo-machete false-positive, and :machete is a blocking gate (SMA-375). paigasus-kernel is
# called directly and needs no ignore.
ignored = ["pyo3"]

[lints]
workspace = true
=== py-bindings moon.yml ===
$schema: 'https://moonrepo.dev/schemas/project.json'

id: 'paigasus-py-bindings-rs'
# Moon-side layer label for this FFI crate (no native `binding` layer exists).
# Built like a library but NOT published as an rlib — ships as a Python wheel
# via maturin. Exclude from any layer=library publish matrix.
layer: 'library'
language: 'rust'

# The kernel→binding edge (ADR-0005): a kernel change must rebuild this crate. `dependsOn`
# creates the project edge; the task-level `^:build` schedules the kernel's build under
# `moon ci --include-relations`. Neither confers affectedness (SMA-389 D3, corrected by
# SMA-524) — that's `@group(upstreams)` below (SMA-528). Mirrors paigasus-node-bindings-rs and
# paigasus-wasm-rs, the other Cargo-backed kernel consumers. NOT paigasus-gateway-rs: that crate's
# kernel edge has no Cargo backing at all and is allowlisted in cargo_moon_parity.py's
# ALLOW_NO_CARGO_BACKING, so it is the opposite case, not a sibling.
dependsOn:
  - 'paigasus-kernel-rs'

# SMA-528 — the transitive dependsOn closure's sources, consumed by build/test/lint via
# `@group(upstreams)` in .moon/tasks/rust.yml. Moon confers affectedness ONLY through a task's own
# `inputs`; dependsOn and `^:build` schedule an upstream but never select this crate. Asserted to
# strict equality by repo:affected-smoke's A6.
fileGroups:
  upstreams:
    - '/rs/crates/libs/paigasus-kernel/src/**/*'
    - '/rs/crates/libs/paigasus-kernel/Cargo.toml'

tasks:
  build:
    deps: ['^:build']
  test:
    deps: ['^:build']
=== rs/.cargo/config.toml ===
# SMA-409/420: the FFI binding cdylibs (paigasus-py-bindings = PyO3 extension-module;
# paigasus-node-bindings = napi-rs) leave their host-runtime symbols intentionally undefined at
# link time — CPython resolves _Py* and Node resolves napi_* when they load the module.
# Linux/ELF permits undefined symbols in shared objects by default; the macOS
# linker rejects them unless told to defer resolution. These flags let `cargo build` link
# the extension on macOS WITHOUT maturin. Scoped to apple-darwin so every other target keeps
# strict link-time symbol checking; CI (Linux) is unaffected.
#
# NOTE: cargo finds this file by walking up from the working directory, so run cargo from
# inside `rs/` (as CONTRIBUTING/CLAUDE.md document, and as `moon` always does). A workspace
# build launched from the repo ROOT won't pick up these flags and fails to link the cdylib
# on macOS with undefined `_Py*` symbols.
[target.x86_64-apple-darwin]
rustflags = ["-C", "link-arg=-undefined", "-C", "link-arg=dynamic_lookup"]

[target.aarch64-apple-darwin]
rustflags = ["-C", "link-arg=-undefined", "-C", "link-arg=dynamic_lookup"]
=== py workspace ===
[tool.uv.workspace]
members = ["packages/*"]

# Python version lives in THREE places that must move together on a floor bump:
# requires-python (per package), tool.basedpyright.pythonVersion, tool.ruff.target-version.
[tool.basedpyright]
typeCheckingMode = "all"
pythonVersion = "3.12"
# Each glob needs a recursive /** suffix: a single-* pattern terminating at a directory
# (packages/*/src) matches the dir but collects NONE of its .py files, so basedpyright runs on
# zero files and the gate passes vacuously (SMA-436). Do not drop the /**.
include = ["packages/*/src/**", "packages/*/tests/**"]
exclude = ["**/__pycache__", "**/node_modules", "**/.venv", "**/dist", "**/build", "**/generated/**"]
reportMissingTypeStubs = "warning"
reportUnnecessaryTypeIgnoreComment = "error"
reportImplicitOverride = "error"
reportImportCycles = "error"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 200
target-version = "py312"
extend-exclude = ["**/generated/**"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "W", "I", "N", "UP", "B", "A", "C4", "SIM", "TCH", "RUF"]
ignore = ["E501"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["packages/*/tests"]
markers = [
  "integration: integration tests that may hit real infrastructure",
  "slow: tests that take more than 1s",
]

# Bounded constraints so a lock regen can't silently bump rule behavior (basedpyright/ruff).
# uv.lock pins the exact resolved versions; these specifiers cap the upgrade window.
[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "anyio[trio]>=4.14.2,<5",
    "basedpyright>=1.39.10,<2",
    "betterproto2-compiler>=0.10,<0.11",
    "pytest>=9.1.1,<10",
    "python-semantic-release>=10.6.1,<11",
    "ruff>=0.16.4,<0.17",
]
=== py tree ===
py:
__pycache__
conftest.py
dist
moon.yml
packages
pyproject.toml
README.md
scripts
uv.lock

py/packages:
paigasus-kernel
paigasus-ml
paigasus-proto
paigasus-workflows

[project]
name = "paigasus-kernel"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Python bindings for the Paigasus behavioral kernel."
readme = "README.md"
license = "Apache-2.0"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
authors = [{ name = "Paigasus contributors" }]
requires-python = ">=3.12"
classifiers = [
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
  "Intended Audience :: Developers",
  "Operating System :: OS Independent",
  "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries",
  "Typing :: Typed",
]
# Pinned exactly, and asserted by repo:version-lockstep. [tool.uv.sources] below is
# DEVELOPMENT-ONLY metadata — uv strips it from the built wheel — so without this pin the
# published wrapper would float against any paigasus-py-bindings version (SMA-576, spec §4).
# Under lockstep the bindings can never release independently, so an exact pin costs nothing.
dependencies = ["paigasus-py-bindings==0.1.0"]

[build-system]
requires = ["uv_build>=0.12.5,<0.13"]
build-backend = "uv_build"

[tool.uv.sources]
paigasus-py-bindings = { path = "../../../rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-py-bindings" }
=== py/moon.yml ===
$schema: 'https://moonrepo.dev/schemas/project.json'

layer: 'configuration'
language: 'python'

# The inherited fileGroups from .moon/tasks/python.yml assume src/ at the project root.
# The py workspace keeps sources under packages/*/src, so extend the inherited groups here.
# Moon merges (not overrides) fileGroups across the layers, so the resolved @group(sources)/
# @group(tests) used by the root's whole-tree checks (lint/fmt/typecheck/test) cover
# packages/*/src/** and packages/*/tests/**.
fileGroups:
  sources:

{"id":"SMA-578","title":"Release activation C: maturin cross-platform wheel matrix for paigasus-py-bindings","description":"Third increment of <issue id="d81426f7-9563-4632-ad1b-b5dd4d0b57c4" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-407/release-activation-000-010-floor-kernelproto-lockstep-wiring-live">SMA-407</issue>, per §7 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-sma-407-release-activation-design.md`.

## The gap

`rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-py-bindings/pyproject.toml` carries a standing caveat: a published **sdist** would not carry `rs/.cargo/config.toml`, whose apple-darwin `-undefined dynamic_lookup` flags the `extension-module` cdylib needs to link. So a macOS consumer building from sdist fails.

The design's answer was "wheels only, no sdist" — but **no maturin wheel matrix exists**. `prebuild.yml`'s 6-leg matrix builds the **napi addon**, not wheels; there is no cibuildwheel or maturin-action anywhere in the repo.

A single-runner build yields one manylinux-x86_64 wheel. With no sdist there is no fallback, so `pip install paigasus-kernel` — which the lockstep pins `==` to `paigasus-py-bindings` — **fails outright on macOS, Windows and linux-aarch64**.

## Scope

Either:

1. **A maturin wheel matrix** (decide the triples; <issue id="639b01a8-3b9b-4521-8ca7-dad37ba37f82" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-428/napi-rs-cross-platform-node-prebuild-matrix-npm-publish-for">SMA-428</issue>'s napi matrix is the shape and the precedent — it settled musl-via-cargo-zigbuild, the macos-13 → macos-15-intel retirement, and the GitHub-bans-JS-actions-in-Alpine-on-arm64 trap), **or**
2. **Publish an sdist and solve the** `rs/.cargo/config.toml` **problem properly** — maturin can include it via `[tool.maturin]` config.

Also in scope: `paigasus-py-bindings/pyproject.toml` has essentially no PyPI metadata (no `description`, `readme`, `license-files`, `authors`, `classifiers`) and the crate dir has no `LICENSE` or `README.md` — contrast `py/packages/paigasus-proto/pyproject.toml:4-17`. Nothing gates PyPI metadata the way `repo:publish-metadata` gates [crates.io](<http://crates.io>); decide whether to extend the gate or accept the asymmetry explicitly.

## Size

Comparable to <issue id="639b01a8-3b9b-4521-8ca7-dad37ba37f82" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-428/napi-rs-cross-platform-node-prebuild-matrix-npm-publish-for">SMA-428</issue>. This is why it is not folded into <issue id="58a95803-beac-456d-90da-1b13eec12279" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-576/release-activation-a-kernel-family-010-floor-repoversion-lockstep-gate">SMA-576</issue>.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-578-release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for","createdAt":"2026-08-22T18:25:55.056Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-28T11:40:17.770Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":"2026-08-28T11:40:17.748Z","canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"In Progress","statusType":"started","labels":["area:release","area:ci"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","assignee":"Sven Maschek","assigneeId":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","parentId":"SMA-407","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

The design's answer was "wheels only, no sdist" — but **no maturin wheel matrix exists**. `prebuild.yml`'s 6-leg matrix builds the **napi addon**, not wheels; there is no cibuildwheel or maturin-action anywhere in the repo.

A single-runner build yields one manylinux-x86_64 wheel. With no sdist there is no fallback, so `pip install paigasus-kernel` — which the lockstep pins `==` to `paigasus-py-bindings` — **fails outright on macOS, Windows and linux-aarch64**.

## Scope

Either:

1. **A maturin wheel matrix** (decide the triples; <issue id="639b01a8-3b9b-4521-8ca7-dad37ba37f82" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-428/napi-rs-cross-platform-node-prebuild-matrix-npm-publish-for">SMA-428</issue>'s napi matrix is the shape and the precedent — it settled musl-via-cargo-zigbuild, the macos-13 → macos-15-intel retirement, and the GitHub-bans-JS-actions-in-Alpine-on-arm64 trap), **or**
2. **Publish an sdist and solve the** `rs/.cargo/config.toml` **problem properly** — maturin can include it via `[tool.maturin]` config.

Also in scope: `paigasus-py-bindings/pyproject.toml` has essentially no PyPI metadata (no `description`, `readme`, `license-files`, `authors`, `classifiers`) and the crate dir has no `LICENSE` or `README.md` — contrast `py/packages/paigasus-proto/pyproject.toml:4-17`. Nothing gates PyPI metadata the way `repo:publish-metadata` gates [crates.io](<http://crates.io>); decide whether to extend the gate or accept the asymmetry explicitly.

## Size

Comparable to <issue id="639b01a8-3b9b-4521-8ca7-dad37ba37f82" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-428/napi-rs-cross-platform-node-prebuild-matrix-npm-publish-for">SMA-428</issue>. This is why it is not folded into <issue id="58a95803-beac-456d-90da-1b13eec12279" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-576/release-activation-a-kernel-family-010-floor-repoversion-lockstep-gate">SMA-576</issue>.","projectMilestone":{"id":"0bc8770f-896e-40bc-a156-e0f92b23faf1","name":"MVP"},"priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-578/release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for-paigasus","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-578-release-activation-c-maturin-cross-platform-wheel-matrix-for","createdAt":"2026-08-22T18:25:55.056Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-28T11:40:17.770Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":"2026-08-28T11:40:17.748Z","canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"In Progress","statusType":"started","labels":["area:release","area:ci"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","assignee":"Sven Maschek","assigneeId":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Polyglot","projectId":"94351cc4-6a23-4c34-a043-2e7f1bfd9ae4","parentId":"SMA-407","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by classifying how much process the request needs, then work
through your path: understand the context, refine the idea, present a
design, and get your human partner's approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any
project, or take any implementation action until you have told your
human partner what you intend and they have approved it. This applies
to EVERY task on EVERY path below — the ceremony scales with the task;
the approval gate never does.
</HARD-GATE>

## Three Paths

Before your first question, classify the request and say the
classification out loud — "this looks bounded, so I'll present a short
design here rather than write a spec" — so your human partner can
override it:

- **Spike** — a feasibility question ("can we...", "is it possible...",
  "quick and dirty is fine") whose output is an answer, not code you
  keep. Present the question and what you'll try in 2-3 sentences, get
  a nod, then find out as cheaply as correctness allows. No design
  doc, no spec file. Report findings as a recommendation; anything you
  built stays labeled throwaway.
- **Bounded** — a well-scoped change to code that already exists in
  this repo: a new flag, a small endpoint, a one-file fix.
  Understanding the kind of app is not enough — bounded means the flow
  you are changing is already here to read. If there is no existing
  flow to change, the task is not bounded. Ask the clarifying
  questions that matter, present a short design IN CHAT (a few
  sentences to a few short paragraphs), and STOP. Implementation
  starts only after your human partner says yes to that design — a
  bounded task's approval is as hard a gate as an architectural
  one. No spec file, no implementation plan document.
- **Architectural** — new projects, new subsystems, changes that
  restructure how components fit together or alter interfaces others
  depend on. Follow the full process: questions, approaches, sectioned
  design, written spec, then the writing-plans skill.

When in doubt between two paths, take the heavier one. The ratchet is
one-way: hidden complexity discovered mid-task upgrades the path —
stop, say so, and step up. Nothing downgrades mid-task.

## Anti-Pattern: "Too Simple To Need Approval"

Every path ends with your human partner approving your intent before
implementation. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config
change — the design may be two sentences in chat, but you MUST present
it and get approval. "Simple" tasks are where unexamined assumptions
cause the most wasted work. What scales with simplicity is the
artifact, never the approval.

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is too simple to need a design" | Simple means a short design, not no design. Two sentences in chat, then approval. |
| "I'll call it bounded and skip the spec" | Reaching for a label to skip work IS the doubt — take the heavier path. |
| "It's bounded and the design is obvious — I'll start while they read it" | The gate is the approval, not the design's length. Present, then stop until you hear yes. |
| "I understand this kind of app, so it's bounded" | Bounded measures the repo, not your familiarity. A new project has no existing flow — it is architectural. |
| "The spike works, so I'll keep the code" | A spike's output is an answer. Keeping the code is a new request — classify it. |
| "It grew, but I'm almost done — no need to re-classify" | Hidden complexity upgrades the path mid-task. Stop and say so. |
| "They approved the spike, so the follow-up change is approved too" | Each task gets its own classification and its own approval. |

## Checklist

Classify first, announce the path, then create a task for each item on
your path and complete them in order.

**Spike:**
1. **Explore project context** — enough to frame the probe
2. **Present question + probe plan** — 2-3 sentences
3. **Get approval** — a nod is enough
4. **Investigate** — as cheaply as correctness allows
5. **Report findings** — a recommendation; label anything built as throwaway

**Bounded:**
1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, the ones that matter
3. **Present short design in chat** — approach, files touched, testing
4. **Get approval** — STOP and wait for an explicit yes; presenting the design and starting in the same breath is skipping the gate
5. **Implement** — proceed with the normal development workflow (TDD applies); no plan document

**Architectural:**
1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Offer the visual companion just-in-time** — NOT upfront. The first time a question would genuinely be clearer shown than described, offer it then (its own message); on approval its browser tab opens for you. If no visual question ever arises, never offer it. See the Visual Companion section below.
3. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
5. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
7. **Spec self-review** — quick inline check for placeholders, contradictions, ambiguity, scope (see below)
8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding
9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot
digraph brainstorming {
    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" [shape=diamond];
    "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" [shape=box];
    "Present short design in chat" [shape=box];
    "Human approves?" [shape=diamond];
    "Investigate; report recommendation" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Implement via normal workflow (no plan doc)" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" [shape=box];
    "User reviews spec?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Hidden complexity? Upgrade path" [shape=box];

    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" [label="spike"];
    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" [label="bounded"];
    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Explore project context" [label="architectural"];
    "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" -> "Human approves?";
    "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" -> "Present short design in chat";
    "Present short design in chat" -> "Human approves?";
    "Human approves?" -> "Investigate; report recommendation" [label="spike: yes"];
    "Human approves?" -> "Implement via normal workflow (no plan doc)" [label="bounded: yes"];
    "Hidden complexity? Upgrade path" -> "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural";
    "Explore project context" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
    "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
    "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";
    "User approves design?" -> "Present design sections" [label="no, revise"];
    "User approves design?" -> "Write design doc" [label="yes"];
    "Write design doc" -> "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)";
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" -> "User reviews spec?";
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Write design doc" [label="changes requested"];
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill" [label="approved"];
}
```

**Terminal states are path-bound.** Architectural: the ONLY skill you
invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans — never frontend-design,
mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. Bounded: after
approval, implementation proceeds directly through the normal
development workflow; no plan document. Spike: the terminal state is a
reported recommendation.

## The Process

The subsections below serve the bounded and architectural paths (a
spike stops at "present the probe, get a nod"). Sections from
**Exploring approaches** onward are architectural-path depth — for
bounded work, context plus a few questions plus a short in-chat design
is the whole process.

**Understanding the idea:**

- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Before asking detailed questions, assess scope: if the request describes multiple independent subsystems (e.g., "build a platform with chat, file storage, billing, and analytics"), flag this immediately. Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs to be decomposed first.
- If the project is too large for a single spec, help the user decompose into sub-projects: what are the independent pieces, how do they relate, what order should they be built? Then brainstorm the first sub-project through the normal design flow. Each sub-project gets its own spec → plan → implementation cycle.
- For appropriately-scoped projects, ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**

- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why
- YAGNI ruthlessly - remove unnecessary features from every approach and design

**Presenting the design:**

- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

**Design for isolation and clarity:**

- Break the system into smaller units that each have one clear purpose, communicate through well-defined interfaces, and can be understood and tested independently
- For each unit, you should be able to answer: what does it do, how do you use it, and what does it depend on?
- Can someone understand what a unit does without reading its internals? Can you change the internals without breaking consumers? If not, the boundaries need work.
- Smaller, well-bounded units are also easier for you to work with - you reason better about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. When a file grows large, that's often a signal that it's doing too much.

**Working in existing codebases:**

- Explore the current structure before proposing changes. Follow existing patterns.
- Where existing code has problems that affect the work (e.g., a file that's grown too large, unclear boundaries, tangled responsibilities), include targeted improvements as part of the design - the way a good developer improves code they're working in.
- Don't propose unrelated refactoring. Stay focused on what serves the current goal.

## After the Design (architectural path)

**Documentation:**

- Write the validated design (spec) to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
  - (User preferences for spec location override this default)
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Spec Self-Review:**
After writing the spec document, look at it with fresh eyes:

1. **Placeholder scan:** Any "TBD", "TODO", incomplete sections, or vague requirements? Fix them.
2. **Internal consistency:** Do any sections contradict each other? Does the architecture match the feature descriptions?
3. **Scope check:** Is this focused enough for a single implementation plan, or does it need decomposition?
4. **Ambiguity check:** Could any requirement be interpreted two different ways? If so, pick one and make it explicit.

Fix any issues inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on.

**User Review Gate:**
After the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:

> "Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan."

Wait for the user's response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.

**Implementation:**

- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

## Visual Companion

A browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool — not a mode. Accepting the companion means it's available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.

**Offering the companion (just-in-time):** Do NOT offer it upfront. Wait until a question would genuinely be clearer shown than told — a real mockup / layout / diagram question, not merely a UI *topic*. The first time that happens, offer it then, as its own message:
> "This next part might be easier if I show you — I can put together mockups, diagrams, and comparisons in a browser tab as we go. It's still new and can be token-intensive. Want me to? I'll open it for you."

**This offer MUST be its own message.** Only the offer — no clarifying question, summary, or other content. Wait for the user's response. If they accept, start the server with `--open` so their browser opens to the first screen automatically. If they decline, continue text-only and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per-question decision:** Even after the user accepts, decide FOR EACH QUESTION whether to use the browser or the terminal. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**

- **Use the browser** for content that IS visual — mockups, wireframes, layout comparisons, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual designs
- **Use the terminal** for content that is text — requirements questions, conceptual choices, tradeoff lists, A/B/C/D text options, scope decisions

A question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question. "What does personality mean in this context?" is a conceptual question — use the terminal. "Which wizard layout works better?" is a visual question — use the browser.

If they agree to the companion, read the detailed guide before proceeding:
`skills/brainstorming/visual-companion.md`

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
name: release

# Only the RELEASE-PR half is live (SMA-576). The release job — tags + registry publishes —
# lands with SMA-580 behind `vars.PAIGASUS_RELEASE_ENABLED`. Nothing here publishes.
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

# release-plz force-updates its PR branch on every run, so two rapid merges to main would
# race. Do NOT cancel in progress: a cancelled run can leave the branch half-written.
concurrency:
  group: release-pr
  cancel-in-progress: false

# Least privilege for the auto GITHUB_TOKEN, matching every other workflow here: it is never
# used for the push/PR below (that goes through secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN — see Checkout).
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  release-pr:
    name: release PR
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      # RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN does not exist yet (a human must create it — see the workflow's
      # own doc). A job-level `if:` cannot see whether it's set: per GitHub's own context-
      # availability table, `jobs.<job_id>.if` only sees github/needs/vars/inputs, never
      # secrets. A step's `if:`/`env:` CAN see secrets, so every step below is individually
      # guarded on this step's output instead. Left unconfigured, this makes the whole job
      # skip cleanly (green) on every push to main instead of failing loudly forever.
      - name: Check for the release-plz token
        id: preflight
        env:
          TOKEN_SET: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN != '' }}
        run: |
          echo "configured=$TOKEN_SET" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ "$TOKEN_SET" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN is not set — skipping the release-PR job until a human creates it (see release.yml)."
          fi

      - name: Checkout
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # persist-credentials: false, matching every other checkout in this repo
          # (artipacked hardening). An earlier revision persisted the App token here so the
          # stamping step could push — but `actions/checkout` writes that credential into
          # the local git config for the WHOLE job, which handed a write-capable token to
          # four steps that have no business with it (setup-toolchain, proto install,
          # moon setup, pnpm install). A compromised action or transitive dependency in any
          # of them could have used it before release work even began.
          #
          # The token now reaches only the two steps that genuinely need it, via their own
          # `env:` — release-plz (GIT_TOKEN) and the stamping step (which authenticates its
          # fetch/push through an explicit remote URL rather than ambient git config).
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up proto + Moon
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095  # v0
        with:
          # Don't cache the proto/Moon toolchain dir: a restored ~/.proto carries stale
          # setup-state that makes `moon setup` skip installing node/pnpm (their shims
          # then don't exist). Reinstall fresh each run (matches ci.yml/prebuild.yml).
          cache: false

      # release-plz is proto-pinned like every other CLI this repo depends on
      # (.prototools, .proto/plugins/release-plz.toml) — install the pinned binary
      # directly rather than through a third-party GitHub Action, which would resolve
      # its own, unpinned release-plz build. Narrow install (not a bare `proto install`):
      # this job needs none of actionlint/buf/deny/machete/nextest/promtool/wasm-pack.
      - name: Install pinned release-plz CLI
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        run: proto install release-plz

      - name: Install Moon-managed toolchains (node, pnpm, rust, python, uv)

      # RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN does not exist yet (a human must create it — see the workflow's
      # own doc). A job-level `if:` cannot see whether it's set: per GitHub's own context-
      # availability table, `jobs.<job_id>.if` only sees github/needs/vars/inputs, never
      # secrets. A step's `if:`/`env:` CAN see secrets, so every step below is individually
      # guarded on this step's output instead. Left unconfigured, this makes the whole job
      # skip cleanly (green) on every push to main instead of failing loudly forever.
      - name: Check for the release-plz token
        id: preflight
        env:
          TOKEN_SET: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN != '' }}
        run: |
          echo "configured=$TOKEN_SET" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ "$TOKEN_SET" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN is not set — skipping the release-PR job until a human creates it (see release.yml)."

          # (artipacked hardening). An earlier revision persisted the App token here so the
          # stamping step could push — but `actions/checkout` writes that credential into
          # the local git config for the WHOLE job, which handed a write-capable token to
          # four steps that have no business with it (setup-toolchain, proto install,
          # moon setup, pnpm install). A compromised action or transitive dependency in any
          # of them could have used it before release work even began.

          # `env:` — release-plz (GIT_TOKEN) and the stamping step (which authenticates its

          # setup-state that makes `moon setup` skip installing node/pnpm (their shims
          # then don't exist). Reinstall fresh each run (matches ci.yml/prebuild.yml).

      # (.prototools, .proto/plugins/release-plz.toml) — install the pinned binary
      # directly rather than through a third-party GitHub Action, which would resolve
      # its own, unpinned release-plz build. Narrow install (not a bare `proto install`):
      # this job needs none of actionlint/buf/deny/machete/nextest/promtool/wasm-pack.
      - name: Install pinned release-plz CLI
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        run: proto install release-plz

      - name: Install Moon-managed toolchains (node, pnpm, rust, python, uv)

=== release.yml tail ===
      - name: Install Moon-managed toolchains (node, pnpm, rust, python, uv)
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        run: moon setup

      - name: Install JS workspace deps
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        run: pnpm --dir ts install --frozen-lockfile

      # release-plz first, ALWAYS, then --write (next step). release-plz owns every Cargo
      # version and the [workspace.dependencies] requirements; --write then brings the six
      # sites it cannot reach (pyproject/package.json/the dependency pin) plus the three
      # regenerated sites into line.
      #
      # Run from rs/: release-plz's config/manifest discovery (./release-plz.toml,
      # ./Cargo.toml) is CWD-relative with no upward search, so this is what makes it find
      # rs/release-plz.toml and rs/Cargo.toml without --config/--manifest-path flags.
      #
      # `--output json` always prints one line, `{"prs": [...]}`, with 0 or 1 elements —
      # verified against the pinned 0.3.158 source
      # (release_plz_core::command::release_pr::release_pr returns Option<ReleasePr>;
      # main.rs wraps None as `[]`, Some(pr) as `[pr]`). Each element carries head_branch/
      # base_branch/html_url/number/releases (the ReleasePr struct) — the CLI's own --help
      # only promises "prints the branch, URL and number", so this was confirmed by reading
      # the source at the exact pinned tag, not assumed from the docs.
      - name: Open or update the release PR
        id: release_pr
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        working-directory: rs
        env:
          GIT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          OUT="$(release-plz release-pr --output json)"
          echo "$OUT"
          echo "json=$OUT" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # release-plz does ALL of its work — version bumps, changelog, branch creation, push —
      # inside a private copy under a tempdir
      # (release_plz_core::command::release_pr::copy_to_temp_dir, confirmed by reading the
      # pinned 0.3.158 source and independently measured: a throwaway clone's HEAD and
      # working tree were untouched after a real `release-pr` run). This checkout's `main`
      # is therefore NEVER the branch to act on — the branch comes only from the JSON above,
      # never from `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` (which would still read "main" here and
      # push straight to it).
      - name: Stamp the non-Cargo manifests onto the release PR branch
        if: steps.preflight.outputs.configured == 'true'
        env:
          PR_JSON: ${{ steps.release_pr.outputs.json }}
          # Scoped to this step only. The checkout sets persist-credentials: false, so there
          # are no ambient git credentials — the fetch and push below authenticate through an
          # explicit remote URL built from this value. GitHub masks the secret in logs, and
          # the URL is never written to git config (no `remote set-url`), so it does not
          # outlive the commands themselves.
          GH_TOKEN_FOR_PUSH: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          PR_COUNT="$(printf '%s' "$PR_JSON" | jq '.prs | length')"
          if [ "$PR_COUNT" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "release-plz: no release PR needed (every releasable package is already" \
                 "at its proposed version) — nothing to stamp"
            exit 0
          fi
          BRANCH="$(printf '%s' "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.prs[0].head_branch')"
          AUTH_REMOTE="REDACTED"

          git fetch "$AUTH_REMOTE" "$BRANCH"
          git checkout -B "$BRANCH" FETCH_HEAD

          bash ci/version-lockstep/run.sh --write

          if git diff --quiet; then
            echo "version-lockstep: nothing to stamp"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name  "paigasus-release[bot]"
          git config user.email "paigasus-release[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add -A
          git commit -m "chore(rs): stamp the non-Cargo manifests to the release version"
          git push "$AUTH_REMOTE" "HEAD:$BRANCH"

content.content:
=== py kernel moon.yml ===
$schema: 'https://moonrepo.dev/schemas/project.json'

id: 'paigasus-kernel-py'
layer: 'library'
language: 'python'

# Cross-language edge to the PyO3 wheel crate (ADR-0005). dependsOn here buys two things:
# build ordering (paigasus-py-bindings-rs:build runs first) and affected-graph propagation
# under `moon ci --include-relations` — the task-level `^:build` is what carries the cascade;
# a project dependsOn alone does not (SMA-389 D3). It does NOT provision the Rust toolchain
# for this project (verified: these tasks resolve to python/uv toolchains only); cargo must be
# on PATH (CI proto shims / dev shell) when `uv sync --reinstall-package` triggers maturin (S6).
dependsOn:
  - 'paigasus-py-bindings-rs'

tasks:
  build:
    deps: ['^:build']
  # Dedicated runtime FFI smoke test. It lives here (not only in the whole-tree py:test) so the
  # kernel→bindings→py cascade actually re-runs it on a Rust edit (review F4). uv serves a CACHED
  # maturin wheel and ignores Rust source changes (spike S4), so we MUST force a rebuild with
  # --reinstall-package before pytest — otherwise this would assert against a stale wheel.
  #
  # `touch` the kernel + binding sources first: maturin's underlying cargo is mtime-incremental, so
  # after a git op that leaves a Rust source OLDER than an existing rs/target/ artifact (warm cache +
  # checkout/rebase/stash → mtime inversion), cargo reports "up to date" and maturin re-links a STALE
  # .so into the freshly reinstalled wheel — the runtime guard then asserts against the wrong kernel
  # (SMA-420's review reproduced sum(2,3)→6 against an `a + b` kernel). Bumping the two (tiny) crates'
  # source mtime forces a content-correct recompile from current source — the py analog of the ts
  # `touch` (SMA-430). `touch` is host-agnostic (CI is Linux, dev is macOS); a per-triple
  # `cargo clean --target <triple>` would have to know the host triple (maturin builds into the
  # per-triple subdir), so we avoid it. Only `test` carries the touch — the `build` task above
  # neither materializes nor asserts the wheel, so it cannot serve a stale artifact (intentional
  # asymmetry with the ts side, whose `build` produces the .node).
  test:
    script: 'touch ../../../rs/crates/libs/paigasus-kernel/src/lib.rs ../../../rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-py-bindings/src/lib.rs && uv sync --reinstall-package paigasus-py-bindings && uv run pytest tests'
    deps: ['^:build']
    inputs:
      - 'tests/**/*'
      - 'src/**/*'
      - 'pyproject.toml'
      - '/py/uv.lock'
      # Both Rust sources: maturin recompiles the binding AND the kernel it calls, so a kernel-source
      # edit must bust this task's Moon cache too (review F4) — Moon hashes only listed inputs, and an
      # upstream `^:build` recompile alone does not re-key this task.
      - '/rs/crates/libs/paigasus-kernel/src/**/*'
      - '/rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-py-bindings/src/**/*'
      # ...and the binding's manifests, so a maturin-config (pyproject.toml) or dependency
      # (Cargo.toml) change re-keys the guard even without a Rust src diff (cache-input completeness).
      - '/rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-py-bindings/Cargo.toml'
      - '/rs/crates/bindings/paigasus-py-bindings/pyproject.toml'
      # Parity corpus (SMA-433): a corpus change must re-run the py replay. This is a task-hash
      # input only — it does NOT make this project affected by a corpus-only edit (see affected-smoke
      # parity-oneway).
      - '/rs/crates/libs/paigasus-kernel-parity/vectors/**/*'
      #
      # Workspace-level Rust files (SMA-546) — see ts/packages/paigasus-kernel/moon.yml's `build`
      # for the full rationale. `--reinstall-package` forces maturin to relink the cdylib, so this
      # task's result depends on the resolution these files pin. `/.prototools` on THIS path pins
      # `uv` (which drives maturin) rather than wasm-pack — nothing on the py path invokes wasm-pack.
      - '/rs/Cargo.lock'
      - '/rs/Cargo.toml'
      - '/rs/rust-toolchain.toml'
      - '/.prototools'
=== python task defs ===
$schema: 'https://moonrepo.dev/schemas/tasks.json'

# Whole-tree quality checks for the py workspace. Scoped to the configuration-layer root
# (py/moon.yml) ONLY: ruff/basedpyright/pytest all read the central config in py/pyproject.toml,
# so one run from py/ covers (and de-duplicates) the whole packages/* tree — running them
# per-package would re-do the same whole-tree work N times (SMA-401). Per-distribution `build`
# lives in python-project.yml.
#
# fileGroups live in each scoped task file (next to the tasks that use them), NOT in the global
# .moon/tasks.yml: Moon 2.2.5 does not propagate global-file fileGroups to projects that inherit
# a task from a scoped file. py/moon.yml extends these with packages/*/src for the root checks.
inheritedBy:
  languages: ['python']
  layers: ['configuration']

fileGroups:
  sources:
    - 'src/**/*'
  tests:
    - 'tests/**/*'
    - '**/*_test.py'
    - '**/test_*.py'

tasks:
  lint:
    command: 'uv run ruff check .'
    inputs: ['@group(sources)', '@group(tests)', 'pyproject.toml', '/py/uv.lock']
  fmt:
    command: 'uv run ruff format --check .'
    inputs: ['@group(sources)', '@group(tests)', 'pyproject.toml', '/py/uv.lock']
  typecheck:
    # `script` (not `command`) because we chain two steps. First run: basedpyright's native
    # output, which fails on real type errors. Second run: --outputjson piped to the coverage
    # guard, which fails if basedpyright analyzed fewer files than the source tree contains --
    # so an include/layout regression can't silently re-darken the gate, totally or partially
    # (SMA-436). If the first run fails, the && short-circuits before the guard runs; otherwise the
    # guard is the last command in the pipe, so its exit status is the pipeline's.
    script: 'uv run basedpyright && uv run basedpyright --outputjson | uv run python scripts/assert_typecheck_coverage.py'
    inputs: ['@group(sources)', '@group(tests)', 'pyproject.toml', '/py/uv.lock', 'scripts/**']
  test:
    command: 'uv run pytest'
    inputs: ['@group(sources)', '@group(tests)', 'pyproject.toml', '/py/uv.lock', 'conftest.py']
$schema: 'https://moonrepo.dev/schemas/tasks.json'

# Per-distribution tasks for the py workspace. Scoped to library/application layers ONLY:
# each py/packages/* builds its own wheel via the uv_build backend. NOT routed to the
# configuration root — py/pyproject.toml is a virtual workspace root with no [project] table,

content.text:
I have enough context. Two findings already shape this materially:

- **`pyo3` is already on `abi3-py312`** (`rs/Cargo.toml:102`). So one wheel per *(OS, arch)* covers CPython 3.12+ — the matrix does **not** multiply by Python version. That is the single biggest simplification versus SMA-428's shape.
- **`release.yml` already exists** (SMA-576) with only the `release-pr` job live; the `release` job — tags + registry uploads — is explicitly deferred, and §12 assigns SMA-579 "the `release` job's **npm** path", implying the PyPI path is this issue's.

First question.

questions.question: How far does SMA-578 reach — build-and-verify only, or all the way to a gated publish path in release.yml?

options.label: Matrix + gated publish path (Recommended)
options.description: Build the wheel matrix AND add the PyPI upload path to release.yml behind `if: vars.PAIGASUS_RELEASE_ENABLED == 'true'` — shipped complete but inert, exactly as §7 describes the `release` job. SMA-580 then only flips the variable. This is what §12's "§7's PyPI half" reads as, and it mirrors SMA-579 owning "the release job's npm path".

options.label: Build + verify only
options.description: A wheel matrix that builds and dry-run-verifies every leg (prebuild.yml's shape: no credentials, no upload), leaving the entire PyPI upload path to SMA-580. Smaller PR, but SMA-580 stops being "flip the variable" and becomes real work for two ecosystems.

options.label: Matrix + publish, no gate
options.description: Wire the upload live now. Rejected by ADR-0011 S4 and §7 — the first upload is irreversible — but listing it so the rejection is explicit.

content.text: While that compiles, the independent question — platform coverage.

questions.question: Which platform set should the wheel matrix cover?

options.label: Mirror prebuild.yml's six (Recommended)
options.description: darwin arm64 + x64, win x64-msvc, linux x64/arm64 gnu, linux x64/arm64 musl — the exact set @paigasus/node-bindings ships. One kernel bound to three languages (ADR-0005); asymmetric platform support between the napi and PyO3 faces is a footgun, and abi3 means each is ONE wheel, not one per Python version.

options.label: Six, minus musl
options.description: Drop musllinux_1_2 (both arches). Alpine is far more common for Node containers than for Python, and this repo's own runtime base is a chisel cut of Ubuntu (glibc). Four wheels, less to maintain — but breaks symmetry with the napi face.

options.label: Six, plus win arm64
options.description: Add aarch64-pc-windows-msvc. Windows-on-ARM is growing, and abi3 makes the extra leg cheap — but there is no napi precedent for it and no runner in prebuild.yml, so it is new ground.

content.text:
Three measurements, all decisive:

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `maturin build` from repo root (no `.cargo/config.toml` on the walk) | ✅ links — `cp312-abi3-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl` |
| Control: plain `cargo build`, same cwd/manifest | ❌ `ld: symbol(s) not found` — undefined `_Py*` |
| `maturin sdist` with the workspace path dep | ✅ **vendors `crates/libs/paigasus-kernel/` + `Cargo.lock`**, rewrites the workspace manifest |

So the pyproject caveat's *observation* holds (the sdist carries no `.cargo/config.toml`) but its *conclusion* does not — maturin injects the darwin link args itself. It also surfaced a new finding: the sdist ships **`moon.yml`**, the same repo-internal leak `repo:publish-metadata` Check 2b exists to catch on the Cargo side, because this crate has no `include` allowlist.

questions.question: Given the sdist premise is now measured false — wheels only, or wheels plus a verified sdist?

options.label: Wheels + verified sdist (Recommended)
options.description: Ship both. The sdist demonstrably builds on macOS without .cargo/config.toml and vendors the kernel path dep, so it is a real fallback for every platform the six legs miss (win arm64, s390x/ppc64le, FreeBSD, a future Python that outruns abi3). Cost: it must be PROVEN — a CI leg that builds the sdist, pip-installs it from source into a clean venv and imports it. An unverified sdist is worse than none, since pip falls back to it and then errors mid-install.

options.label: Wheels only, correct the record
options.description: Keep §7's "wheels only" decision, but rewrite the pyproject caveat and the spec to state the real reason (we choose not to make consumers carry a Rust toolchain) rather than the false one (macOS cannot link). Smaller surface; no sdist verification leg. A platform outside the six then has no install path at all.

options.label: sdist only, no matrix
options.description: Drop the matrix entirely now that the sdist works. Rejected: every consumer would need a Rust toolchain and a multi-minute compile on `pip install`. Listed so the rejection is explicit.

questions.question: §14 Q8 — nothing gates PyPI metadata the way repo:publish-metadata gates crates.io. Extend, add, or accept?

options.label: Extend repo:publish-metadata (Recommended)
options.description: Add a Python arm to the gate that already exists: a strict-equality publishable set (paigasus-kernel, paigasus-py-bindings, paigasus-proto), required [project] fields, LICENSE/README present, and an sdist-contents assertion catching the moon.yml leak — the exact mirror of Check 2b. It is already in ci.yml's T array with negative-control and self-test scaffolding, so this costs no new SMA-541/553/530 bookkeeping. Its name is already ecosystem-neutral.

options.label: New repo:pypi-metadata gate
options.description: A separate task with its own script. Cleaner separation of ecosystems and independent `inputs` (a py-only PR would not schedule the Cargo half) — but pays the full new-gate tax: T array, CLAUDE.md markers, input-liveness, SELF_SCHEDULED_GATES, SELF_TASK_EXPECTED_GLOBS, its own negative control.

options.label: Fix metadata, accept asymmetry
options.description: Add the missing description/readme/license-files/authors/classifiers plus LICENSE and README.md by hand, and record in the spec that PyPI metadata is ungated on purpose. Cheapest — but the next binding crate silently repeats the omission, and the moon.yml leak stays uncaught.

questions.question: Where does the six-leg wheel matrix live — and how does release.yml get wheels to upload?

options.label: New reusable wheels.yml (Recommended)
options.description: A new `wheels.yml` mirroring prebuild.yml's shape, with `on: workflow_call` alongside its own pull_request/push triggers. release.yml `uses:` it, then uploads the artifacts it produced. One matrix definition, two consumers — no duplicated six-leg block, and the PR-time verification runs the EXACT job the release path runs. Triggers stay py-specific, so a napi-only change does not build wheels.

options.label: Add wheel legs to prebuild.yml
options.description: Extend the existing matrix so one runner pass builds both the .node and the wheel per target — halves runner-minutes and cache duplication. But prebuild.yml's triggers are deliberately tuned to napi inputs (its own comments say so), so the two faces' trigger sets would fight, and release.yml still needs its own way to obtain wheels.

options.label: Build wheels inline in release.yml
options.description: Put the matrix only in the release job. Smallest file count, but the matrix would then be exercised for the first time on a push to main after merge — no PR-time verification of the thing that actually publishes.

questions.question: How does the gated release job authenticate to PyPI?

options.label: Trusted Publishing / OIDC (Recommended)
options.description: §7 already prefers it. `permissions: id-token: write` + pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish; no long-lived token exists to leak, and release.yml has no pull_request trigger so no PR can reach it either way. Operational cost: a human must create a PENDING publisher on PyPI for each of the two distributions BEFORE the first upload, bound to this repo + the release.yml filename — that becomes a line in SMA-580's pre-flight checklist.

options.label: PYPI_API_TOKEN secret
options.description: A scoped API token in repository secrets. Works immediately with no pre-registration and survives a workflow rename. But it is a long-lived, exfiltratable credential of exactly the class §7's review M2 spent its argument on, and it needs rotation.

options.label: OIDC now, token as documented fallback
options.description: Wire OIDC as the path, but have the job fall back to a token if the secret is set. Rejected as designed-in ambiguity: two auth paths means the untested one is the one that runs in an emergency.

12:#            `cargo publish --dry-run` only WARNS about a missing description, so this
13:#            explicit assertion is the half that actually guards the metadata.
14:#   Check 1b each category is a REAL crates.io slug, validated against the committed
15:#            snapshot ci/publish-metadata/crates-io-categories.txt. crates.io DROPS unknown
16:#            slugs and publishes anyway, and `cargo publish --dry-run` returns before the
17:#            warning that would have said so — so Check 2 cannot catch this (SMA-529).
18:#   Check 1c each publishable crate declares its OWN [lints.*] table and does not deny.
19:#            Cargo inlines the resolved table into the published manifest and docs.rs builds
20:#            on nightly as the root package, where --cap-lints allow does not apply — so an
21:#            inherited (or hand-written) `warnings = "deny"` silently kills docs.rs builds
22:#            on the first new rustc lint, months later (SMA-577).
23:#   Check 1d each publishable crate declares a non-empty `include` ALLOWLIST containing
24:#            README.md and LICENSE. Membership is literal: "**/*" is rejected, because it
25:#            would "cover" both while reinstating the moon.yml leak 2b exists to catch.
26:#   Check 2  `cargo publish --dry-run` succeeds, once per PUBLISH GROUP — a connected
27:#            component of the in-set dependency graph, computed at runtime from `cargo
28:#            metadata` — not once per package: a per-package dry-run of a crate with an
29:#            unpublished in-tree dependency cannot succeed (`-p paigasus-proto` alone exits
30:#            101, `no matching package named 'paigasus-proto-derive'`, until the derive crate
31:#            is on crates.io). The group is publishABLE, packages, and compiles with no
32:#            unversioned path dependency OUTSIDE the group.
33:#   Check 2b the packaged file list ships README.md + LICENSE and not moon.yml.
34:#   Check 2c the packaged set does not contain EVERY tracked file in the crate dir. This is
35:#            Check 1d's rule enforced BEHAVIOURALLY: 1d rejects catch-all `include` entries
36:#            by spelling, and that list can never be complete — /**, /*, **/, /, **/**,
37:#            */**, */*, ?*, [a-z]* and **/*.* were all MEASURED to package a crate's whole
38:#            root, and any glob that happens to match everything joins them. If the allowlist
39:#            held nothing back it matched everything, whatever it was spelled. Note this is a
40:#            SUBSET test, not equality: a catch-all can also sweep untracked files in, making
41:#            the packaged set a strict superset while every tracked file still ships (SMA-577).
42:#   Check 3  while any publishable crate is at 0.0.0, rs/release-plz.toml must block its
43:#            release. Releasing 0.0.0 permanently burns that version on crates.io.
44:#   Check 4  .github/workflows/security-scan.yml still INVOKES the freshness check on a real,
45:#            non-comment run: line whose exit status is not discarded, and does not suppress
46:#            it with continue-on-error or if:. Nothing else guards a workflow job:
47:#            repo:actionlint's call-site machinery is keyed on ci.yml only (SMA-529).
49:# Exit codes: 0 pass | 1 assertion failed (the repo is wrong) | 2 infrastructure failed.
50:# A broken invocation must NEVER read as "all checks passed".
52:# ALL cargo invocations run from rs/. rust-toolchain.toml (1.95.0) and .cargo/config.toml
53:# are discovered by walking up from CWD, NOT from --manifest-path (see the note in
54:# rs/.cargo/config.toml and the E0514 incident recorded in rs/rust-toolchain.toml), and
55:# there is no repo-root Cargo.toml. Every other cargo gate in moon.yml does the same.
63:# The heredocs below `cd` into rs/, so an import cannot rely on CWD. Exported once rather
64:# than per-call so --negative-control's direct function calls see it too.
67:# The ONE maintained fact in this script. SMA-577 added paigasus-proto AND
68:# paigasus-proto-derive here — both, because the derive crate must publish first.
69:EXPECTED_PUBLISHABLE=("paigasus-kernel" "paigasus-proto" "paigasus-proto-derive")
71:# What a published artifact must and must not contain.
75:die_infra() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 2; }
77:# Checks 0, 1 and 3 — pure functions of (cargo metadata JSON, release-plz.toml).
78:# Takes file paths so --negative-control (Task 4) can drive the SAME code with fixtures.
79:# On success prints one "<name>\t<manifest-dir>" line per publishable crate on stdout.

{"id":"SMA-556","title":"py: paigasus-ml and paigasus-workflows declare README.md + LICENSE build inputs that do not exist","description":"## Context

Found while measuring the whole-graph input baseline for <issue id="0ef6ae1f-52d0-43f4-a004-1d58dde354b6" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-553/repo-assert-every-repo-tasks-inputs-still-match-a-file-a-gate-can-be">SMA-553</issue> (recorded as §7 of its design doc).

`.moon/tasks/python-project.yml:27` declares `README.md` and `LICENSE` among the `build` task's inputs, inherited by every python project. For two of them the files **do not exist** — not gitignored, absent:

```
py/packages/paigasus-ml/          -> moon.yml, pyproject.toml, src/
py/packages/paigasus-workflows/   -> moon.yml, pyproject.toml, src/
```

So `moon query projects` reports four declared `inputFiles` with no backing file:

* `paigasus-ml-py:build` :: `py/packages/paigasus-ml/README.md`
* `paigasus-ml-py:build` :: `py/packages/paigasus-ml/LICENSE`
* `paigasus-workflows-py:build` :: `py/packages/paigasus-workflows/LICENSE`
* `paigasus-workflows-py:build` :: `py/packages/paigasus-workflows/README.md`

These are the **only** four untracked file inputs in the entire 119-task graph — every other dead input measured is a speculative convention glob from the language task templates, which are harmless.

## Why it matters

Both packages are PyPI-bound and build with `uv_build` (`build-backend = "uv_build"`). Per <issue id="88063e74-3c5a-46be-9ee6-9e85c7c01426" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-378/add-pypi-publishing-metadata-to-paigasus-proto-and-paigasus-kernel">SMA-378</issue>, `uv_build` **does not auto-glob license files**: a package needs `license-files = ["LICENSE"]` in `pyproject.toml` *and* a real `LICENSE` copy, or the wheel ships no license text at all. Neither package has either.

Latent rather than urgent — no release workflow is wired, and the `[tool.semantic_release]` config in both `pyproject.toml`s is explicitly dormant. But it becomes a real defect the moment either package is published.

## Also a precondition for <issue id="0ef6ae1f-52d0-43f4-a004-1d58dde354b6" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-553/repo-assert-every-repo-tasks-inputs-still-match-a-file-a-gate-can-be">SMA-553</issue>

<issue id="0ef6ae1f-52d0-43f4-a004-1d58dde354b6" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-553/repo-assert-every-repo-tasks-inputs-still-match-a-file-a-gate-can-be">SMA-553</issue>'s gate is deliberately scoped to the `repo` project. Its §6 L1 records that widening to the whole graph requires two things: pruning the dead convention globs from the task templates, **and** fixing these four — because they are genuine defects that would red first. This issue is that second half.

## Acceptance criteria

{"id":"SMA-535","title":"py: py:typecheck does not propagate from Rust, so a PyO3 signature change ships unchecked","description":"Found while scoping <issue id="51c53fdd-c04b-4433-ba69-4648444d50f8" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-526/rust-lintfmt-propagate-across-no-moon-edge-so-a-downstream-clippy">SMA-526</issue> (Rust lint propagation). Same silent-hole shape, one stack over. An early draft of the <issue id="51c53fdd-c04b-4433-ba69-4648444d50f8" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-526/rust-lintfmt-propagate-across-no-moon-edge-so-a-downstream-clippy">SMA-526</issue> spec claimed py/ts had "no analogous hole"; that claim argued from *coverage* when the question is *scheduling*, and was wrong.

## The problem

`py:lint`, `py:typecheck` and `py:test` live on the `py` configuration-root project (`.moon/tasks/python.yml`, scoped `layers: ['configuration']`). That project:

* has **no** `dependsOn` to any Rust project, and
* lists **no** `rs/**` **inputs** on any of those tasks.

So a Rust kernel or binding edit schedules **none** of them.

## What currently closes the gap, and how far it actually reaches

Only `paigasus-kernel-py:test`'s hand-written `/rs/...` inputs (`py/packages/paigasus-kernel/moon.yml`). That is **runtime** coverage via pytest, not type coverage.

`py/packages/paigasus-kernel/src/paigasus_kernel/__init__.py` re-exports symbols from the PyO3 module. A signature or type change that pytest does not happen to exercise is a basedpyright finding that never runs on the PR introducing it — it surfaces later, on an unrelated py change.

## Suggested fix

Either give the `py` root project an edge to the binding crates, or add the relevant `/rs/...` inputs to `py:typecheck` the way `paigasus-kernel-py:test` already does for its own inputs. Note `py:typecheck` is whole-tree (<issue id="9130e7c4-448f-4e2a-b196-d89576e149a4" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-401/moon-root-per-package-whole-tree-tasks-lintfmttypechecktest-re-run">SMA-401</issue>), so propagating it is coarse — weigh the cost as in <issue id="51c53fdd-c04b-4433-ba69-4648444d50f8" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-526/rust-lintfmt-propagate-across-no-moon-edge-so-a-downstream-clippy">SMA-526</issue>.

options.label: Skeleton + PyPI path only (Recommended)

Someone has to create it, and SMA-578 is the first of the three parallel children. Risk: SMA-579 runs in parallel and would conflict on the same file.

content.text:
Confirmed, and it surfaces a real open hole: **`ci/actionlint/run.sh` contains no `PAIGASUS_RELEASE_ENABLED` assertion and `SELF_TEST_COUNT` is still 9.** SMA-576 listed the re-founded release guard in its scope but could not implement it — there was no `release` job to guard. Meanwhile `repo:publish-metadata` Check 3 went **vacuous** the moment the family reached `0.1.0` (it skips when no publishable crate is at `0.0.0`). So right now nothing structurally guards publishing. SMA-578 creates the job, so it inherits that obligation.

---

# Design — SMA-578

### §1 Scope

Seven decisions, all settled above: gated publish path (not build-only) · six platforms mirroring the napi face · **wheels + a verified sdist** · extend `repo:publish-metadata` rather than add a gate · a **reusable** `wheels.yml` · **OIDC** trusted publishing · release-job skeleton with the PyPI path only (npm stays SMA-579's). Plus **SMA-556 folded in**.

### §2 The measurement that redirects the design

The `pyproject.toml` caveat and spec §7/M3 both rest on "a published sdist won't carry `rs/.cargo/config.toml`, so macOS can't link." Measured on this host: maturin built the wheel **from the repo root**, where that file is not on cargo's upward walk; the control — plain `cargo build`, same cwd and manifest — failed with undefined `_Py*`. **maturin injects the darwin link args itself.** `rs/.cargo/config.toml` exists for non-maturin `cargo build`, exactly as its own comment says, and is irrelevant to packaging. So the sdist prohibition is retired and replaced with a *verified* sdist. The spec must correct the record in three places: the pyproject comment, spec §7's M3 paragraph, and §15's risk row.

### §3 `wheels.yml` — reusable build workflow

`on: workflow_call` + `pull_request`/`push`/`workflow_dispatch`, trigger paths mirroring prebuild.yml's discipline (narrow py/maturin inputs pre-merge, `rs/**` post-merge), all as **block sequences** per `repo:actionlint`.

| leg | runner | target(s) | wheel tag |
|---|---|---|---|
| darwin | `macos-latest` | both apple triples in one job | `macosx_11_0_arm64`, `macosx_10_12_x86_64` |
| windows | `windows-latest` | `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` | `win_amd64` |
| linux ×4 | `ubuntu-latest` | gnu/musl × x64/arm64, all `--zig` | `manylinux_2_17_*`, `musllinux_1_2_*` |

Six jobs, seven wheels, all `cp312-abi3` — `abi3-py312` is already on (`rs/Cargo.toml:102`), so there is no per-Python-version multiplication.

**The one place this must diverge from prebuild.yml:** `--zig` on **all four** linux legs, not just musl. `ubuntu-latest` ships glibc 2.39, so a native build tags `manylinux_2_39` — installable almost nowhere. zig retargets glibc 2.17. A happy side effect: no `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners are needed, so this matrix is *cheaper* than prebuild's.

**Tag assertions are exact-equality, never substring** — prebuild's `lipo -archs` lesson (`grep -q x86_64` passes for a fat binary). The exact tag strings get **measured in CI on the first run**, not assumed. Native import-and-call smoke on the three legs whose arch the runner can execute (darwin-arm64, win_amd64, linux-x64-gnu); `lipo`-style inspection of the `.so` inside the darwin-x64 wheel.

### §4 sdist

A seventh job builds `maturin sdist` (verified: it vendors `crates/libs/paigasus-kernel/` + `Cargo.lock` and rewrites the workspace manifest), then in a clean venv `pip install --no-binary :all:` it and imports. An unverified sdist is worse than none — pip falls back to it and fails mid-install. Same job builds `paigasus-kernel`'s pure-Python wheel via `uv build`.

### §5 Packaging metadata

`paigasus-py-bindings`'s wheel `METADATA` is **88 bytes** today. It gains description / readme / license / `license-files` / authors / classifiers following `py/packages/paigasus-proto`'s shape, plus a real `LICENSE` and `README.md`, plus a Cargo `include` allowlist — the sdist currently ships **`moon.yml`**, the identical leak `repo:publish-metadata` Check 2b exists to catch. Edits must not disturb `[project]` coming first, which `ci/version-lockstep/run.sh`'s `write_site` relies on. `py.typed` and `__init__.pyi` already ship correctly — no PEP 561 work.

**Folded SMA-556:** the same treatment for `paigasus-ml` and `paigasus-workflows` (LICENSE + README + `license-files`), honouring SMA-378's rule that an SPDX expression means the `License ::` trove classifier is *omitted*.

### §6 `repo:publish-metadata` grows a Python arm

Discovery rule: **`version != "0.0.0"` ⇒ PyPI-bound** — mirrors ADR-0011 S4's dormant-until-real, needs no new marker, and the two stubs sit at `0.0.0`.

- **P0** publishable set ≡ `EXPECTED_PYPI_PUBLISHABLE=(paigasus-kernel paigasus-py-bindings paigasus-proto)`, strict equality (the non-vacuity control, mirroring Check 0)
- **P1** required `[project]` fields + the SPDX-vs-classifier rule
- **P2** README/LICENSE exist on disk (`uv_build` does not auto-glob — SMA-378)
- **P3** built-artifact contents ship README+LICENSE and **not** `moon.yml` — the behavioural mirror of 2b/2c

The existing `--negative-control` gains py fixtures proving the arm can report red. Task `inputs` grow accordingly, which `repo:input-liveness` then holds live.

### §7 `release.yml` — the gated skeleton

A new `release` job behind `if: vars.PAIGASUS_RELEASE_ENABLED == 'true'`, running `release-plz release` (crates.io + tags), then `uses: ./.github/workflows/wheels.yml`, then a `publish-pypi` job with `permissions: id-token: write` and no long-lived token. **Publish order is `paigasus-py-bindings` before `paigasus-kernel`** — the face pins `==`, so the reverse order leaves it uninstallable in the window between, the same ordering lesson as derive→proto. Nothing publishes until SMA-580 flips the variable.

**Guard-the-guard obligation** (§9's, now unblocked): a new verdict function in `ci/actionlint/run.sh` asserting the `if:` guard exists, references the variable, and is not defeated by `continue-on-error:` or a discarded exit status — plus its own self-test table, `SELF_TEST_COUNT` 9 → 10, and a whole-line `ACTIONLINT_SH_CALL_SITES` entry.

### §8 Folds considered and declined

| Ticket | Why not |
|---|---|
| SMA-535 py:typecheck doesn't propagate from Rust | Moon affected-graph mechanism; re-baselines `ci/affected-graph` strict equality. Different subsystem. |
| SMA-560 wrapper Rust-source inputs unasserted | A different gate with its own bookkeeping tax. |
| SMA-434 FFI glue drift check | napi/wasm, not the PyPI path. |
| SMA-552 `--locked` unenforceable | Touched only incidentally (the sdist embeds `Cargo.lock`). |

### §9 Risks

The wheel tag strings and maturin's `x86_64-apple-darwin` deployment-target default are **assumptions until CI measures them** — the plan must treat the first run as a measurement, not a verification. OIDC needs a *pending publisher* registered on PyPI for both distributions before the first upload; that becomes a line in SMA-580's pre-flight checklist. And `gh workflow run wheels.yml` 404s until `wheels.yml` is on `main` (CLAUDE.md).

---
